name: Long running tasks
description:
1. **Request:** add long‑running tasks — a complex objective is split into sub‑tasks on a dedicated kanban board with a budget and a managing profile, processed until all done / budget exhausted / user stops, and resumable after any restart.
2. **API review:** tasks are chats (`Chat` with `board`/`column`/`status`/`cost`/`estimation_cost`), the board catalogue is `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` (`ChatManager.load_kanban/save_kanban`), budget is already enforced per chat in `smol_agent.py`, cancellation via `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY` + `POST /api/chat/cancel`, and background work runs in daemon threads from `background.py` (not in the 30s‑limited request path).
3. **Proposed design:** a run = board config (`long_run` key) + runtime state in `.codx/long_running/<board_id>.json` with a file lock; a `tick()` runner picks one actionable task at a time, pushes the remaining budget down as `estimation_cost`, and hands control to the supervisor profile when no task is actionable, which alone may call `finish`.
4. **Deliverables:** new `codx/junior/long_running/` (models, store, service, runner), `api/long_running.py` (start/pause/resume/stop/status/tick), `tools/long_running_tools.py`, a supervisor profile, plus patches to `background.py` and `tools/__init__.py`; no changes to `db.py`, `chat_manager.py`, `smol_agent.py` or `planning_manager.py`.
5. **Open before implementation:** budget unit (cxjcoins vs task count), one task at a time vs `max_parallel`, worker inside `background.py` vs an always‑on API thread, and config split across `kanban.json` + state file vs a single file — plus two pre‑existing defects to fix separately (broken `codx/junior/kanban/__init__.py` import, duplicated/legacy handlers in `app.py` and `api/chat.py`).

We need an initial version of long running tasks. Given a complex tasks it will split into small tasks and process. It can generate more tasks as needed.
Goal is to return a (depending on the task) a functional work that user can test and review.

Examples: 
 - "Create a website with a and b that does c"
 - "Review all UI compoenents and generate a catching mobile UI"

We'll create a board for the long running task and assign a budget and a profile to manage the process, all sub tasks generated will be in the same board and the profile will decide when the task is done. Tasks will be processed until:
 -  All tasks are done
 - Board runs out of budget
 - Stopped by user

Long running tasks must be resumed in case of an app reset/power-off. Processing will continue until the conditions are met.

Review all codx-junior API and suggest the best way to implement it.

I'll start by mapping the project and locating the pieces involved in task processing, boards, budgets, and background execution.## 1. Review & Understand the Task **Objective (my reading):** - Introduce **long‑running tasks (LRT)**: one *complex objective* is split into small tasks that are processed one after another, and the run may **generate new tasks** while it goes. - The unit of organisation is a **kanban board**: the board holds the budget and the **profile that manages the process**; all generated sub‑tasks live on that board. - The managing profile is the one that **decides the run is finished**. - Processing continues until: **all tasks done**, **board budget exhausted**, or **stopped by the user**. - The run must **survive an app reset / power‑off** and continue automatically. - Deliverable of this step: **review the existing API and propose the implementation** (not a full code dump). **Acceptance criteria I will hold the design against:** 1. Start a run from a free‑text objective → board + budget + profile are recorded and the run starts by itself. 2. Sub‑tasks are created/updated by the managing profile through existing tooling, all on the run's board. 3. Execution is **out of the request path** (the API has a 30s middleware timeout) and survives restart with no manual "resume" click. 4. Exactly **one** worker advances a given run, even with several API/background processes. 5. Budget is enforced **hard** (never exceeded, not just reported) and accounted even if messages are deleted. 6. Stop/pause is honoured promptly, mid‑turn, and the stopped state is durable. 7. Every tick is observable (chat events + socket + control chat transcript) and cost is attributable per run. --- ## 2. Information Gathering — API review (facts found, with paths) The relevant machinery already exists; LRT should be **composition, not a new subsystem**. Key findings: | Area | Reality in this repo | Consequence for LRT | |---|---|---| | Task = chat | `codx/junior/db.py::Chat` (`board`, `column`, `sprints`, `status`, `mode`, `profiles`, `cost`, `estimation_cost`), persisted as `.codx/tasks///..json` (`chat_manager.py::get_chat_file`) | Sub‑tasks are plain chats; no new entity needed | | Creation core | `codx/junior/task_manager.py::TaskManager.create_task` — mandatory `name`+`description`, nothing inherited | The supervisor must create fully‑specified tasks; no AI auto‑split exists anymore (`ChatEngineActions.generate_tasks` was removed) | | Catalogue | `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` `{version, boards:{name:{id,title,description,columns[{id,title,color}],active,last_update,parent_id,type}}, tags}`; read/write via `ChatManager.load_kanban/save_kanban`; board/column/sprint CRUD + `validate_task_destination` in `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py` | Board entry is the natural place for **run configuration**; board *name* is also the folder (`get_chat_file`) | | Budget primitive | `Chat.estimation_cost` + monotonic `Chat.cost`; enforcement in `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py` (`_cost_limit_exceeded`, `_accumulated_chat_cost`, stops **before** executing more tools, emits `ESTIMATION_COST_EXCEEDED_MSG`); accumulation in `ChatManager.add_message/update_message/_accumulate_message_cost` | Per‑task hard cap already works; the **board** cap must be aggregated and pushed down as `estimation_cost` per task | | Execution entry | `CODXJuniorSession.chat_with_project(chat=...)` → `ChatEngineActions` → `ChatEngine.chat_with_project` (cancellation token registered per `chat.doc_id`, `ChatEventBridge` persists increments) | One "unit of work" = one `chat_with_project` on one task | | Cancellation | `codx/junior/ai/cancellation.py::CANCELLATION_REGISTRY` (by `chat_id` or `token_id`), exposed at `POST /api/chat/cancel` (`codx/junior/api/chat.py`) | "Stop by user" = durable flag **+** cancel the in‑flight token | | Background execution | `codx/junior/background.py`: `start_background_services(stop_event)` starts **daemon threads** only when `CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND` is set; loops use `check_projects` + `ThreadPoolExecutor`; async work is run per thread with `asyncio.run(...)` (`run_project_check_thread`) | The LRT loop belongs here, with a per‑run lock; **the plain API process does not run background loops** | | HTTP constraints | `app.py`: `GLOBAL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30` middleware → 504; routers are **auto‑discovered** (`codx/junior/api/__init__.py::discover_routers`, every module exporting `router` is mounted at `/api`) | LRT endpoints must be **start/stop/status only**; long work never inside the request; new router file is auto‑registered | | Planning/status vocabulary | `codx/junior/planning_manager.py`: `STATUS_ORDER = [todo, doing, onhold, done, rejected]`, `DONE_STATUSES = {done}`, `CLOSED_STATUSES = {done, rejected}`; `ChatStatusEvent` appended on every real transition (`ChatManager._register_status_change`) | "All tasks done" must use **these** constants, never a second list | | UI hooks | `PlanningManager.query_tasks/build_dashboard` (`POST /api/planning/tasks/query`, `/dashboard`), `/api/kanban` GET/POST, `ChatEventBridge` + `message_event` | Board progress and per‑task status are already renderable; only run state needs a new view | **Blocking defects found while reviewing (must be handled before/with LRT):** 1. `codx/junior/kanban/__init__.py` imports `codx.junior.kanban.board_status_review`, **which does not exist in the repo** → `import codx.junior.kanban` raises. LRT must not import that package (and the import should be repaired separately). 2. `codx/junior/app.py` still contains legacy handlers that call removed code (e.g. `/api/chats/sub-tasks` → `codx_junior_session.generate_tasks`) and duplicated `@app.on_event("startup")`. `codx/junior/api/chat.py` also defines `PUT /chats/mark-seen/...` twice. Not caused by LRT, but the LRT router must not add to the drift. 3. `kanban.json` writes are **read‑modify‑write with no lock** (`ChatManager.save_kanban`), while the UI writes the same file. Run *runtime* state must therefore **not** live in `kanban.json`. 4. Board *name* is the storage folder (`get_chat_file`), and `project_manager_tools` still `shutil.move`s folders on rename. Runs should therefore key on the **board `id`** and never trigger renames. --- ## 3. Change Proposal & Refinement ### 3.1 Core idea A **run** is a *board + configuration + durable state machine*, advanced by a **single "tick" at a time**: ```mermaid flowchart TD T[Tick] --> L{lock ok?} L -->|no| X[skip] L -->|yes| S{state RUNNING?} S -->|no| X S -->|yes| B{spent >= budget?} B -->|yes| BE[STOP: budget_exhausted] B -->|no| A{actionable task?} A -->|yes| R[recover/claim task -> estimation_cost = remaining
chat_with_project(task)] R --> U[persist attempt + heartbeat] U --> T2[next tick] A -->|no| SUP[supervisor turn on control chat
create/move/verify tasks, or finish] SUP --> D{finished?} D -->|yes| CP[STOP: completed + delivery report] D -->|no| T2 ``` Why this shape: - **Crash‑safe by construction**: state is on disk, and the only in‑flight unit is one chat turn, which is itself persisted incrementally (`ChatEventBridge.maybe_persist_stream`). A restart resumes the same tick. - **Idempotent**: a tick re‑reads chats from disk; nothing is held in memory between ticks. - **Budget‑honest**: costs are read from `Chat.cost` (monotonic, survives message deletion) and the remaining budget is pushed down into `Chat.estimation_cost` so `SmolAgent` stops the individual turn before overspending. - **No new scheduler**: reuse the existing daemon‑thread + `asyncio.run` pattern; no Celery/APScheduler. ### 3.2 Data model (two stores, on purpose) 1. **Run configuration — board entry in `tasks/kanban.json`** (UI‑editable, already the catalogue): ```json { "id": "uuid", "title": "Website a+c", "type": "long_running", "long_run": { "enabled": true, "objective": "Create a website with a and b that does c", "profile": "tech_lead", "budget_cxjcoins": 25.0, "per_task_budget_cxjcoins": 2.0, "supervisor_reserve_cxjcoins": 2.5, "max_tasks": 40, "max_iterations": 200, "task_mode": "agent", "column": "tasks", "verify_column": "review", "created_at": "...", "created_by": "user@x" } } ``` 2. **Run runtime state — separate file** `.codx/long_running/.json` (atomic `os.replace`, own lock), so UI edits of `kanban.json` never race: ```python LongRunState: board_id, board, status (running|paused|stopped|completed|budget_exhausted|failed|stalled) attempts: {task_id: int} current_task_id, step_started_at, last_tick_at, ticks spent_cxjcoins (checkpoint; recomputed from chats each tick) stop_reason, summary, delivery_report_message_id lock: {pid, host, heartbeat_at} ``` ### 3.3 Loop and stop conditions - **Actionable task** = `status in (todo, doing)` on the board with `attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS (3)`, ordered `priority, due_date, sort_index`. Exactly **one at a time** per run (predictable budget, no worktree/board contention). `max_parallel` can be added later behind the same tick. - **Recovery**: if `current_task_id` is set, the process died, and no `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY` token exists → `attempts += 1`, re‑run. After `MAX_ATTEMPTS` → `status="onhold"` + supervisor comment (`project_manager(action='request_help')`). - **Budget**: `spent = Σ chat.cost` over chats on the board **including the control chat**; before each turn ensure `spent < budget`, else `budget_exhausted`. Because the supervisor also costs money, `supervisor_reserve_cxjcoins` is kept aside so the run can always produce the final report. - **Completion**: only the **managing profile** may finish, via an explicit tool call (`long_running(action="finish", summary=...)`). Safety nets: `stalled` after `STAGNATION_TICKS` (e.g. 3) supervisor turns that neither create nor move a task, `failed` on unrecoverable errors, `max_tasks/max_iterations` guards against infinite self‑expansion. - **User stop/pause**: written to state (durable) **and** `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY.cancel(current_task_id)` to abort mid‑turn. `resume` clears the flag; nothing else is recreated. ### 3.4 Execution placement & single‑worker guarantee - New loop `check_long_running_runs()` in `background.py`, own thread, interval ~5s, started next to `check_projects` (same `RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES` flag, same "runs in the background process" contract). Each run advances inside its own thread with `asyncio.run(runner.tick())`, mirroring `run_project_check_thread`. - **Single worker**: lock file `.codx/long_running/.lock` created with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` containing `{pid, host}`; a stale lock (heartbeat older than `LOCK_TIMEOUT`, e.g. 10 min) is taken over. This is what makes restart recovery and multi‑process safe. ### 3.5 API surface (follows the project REST conventions) Identity in the URL (`board_id`), `project_id` as **query** param, bodies describe the resource only: | Method | Path | Body / effect | |---|---|---| | `GET` | `/api/long-running` | list runs (config + state + progress/budget) | | `POST` | `/api/long-running` | `{objective, budget_cxjcoins, profile, board?, column?, task_mode?, max_tasks?, max_iterations?, per_task_budget_cxjcoins?, supervisor_reserve_cxjcoins?, auto_start?}` → creates board (via catalogue helpers) + control chat + state | | `GET` | `/api/long-running/{board_id}` | detail (state, spent/remaining, task counts, current task) | | `POST` | `/api/long-running/{board_id}/pause` \| `/resume` \| `/stop` | durable flag (+ cancel in‑flight token on stop) | | `POST` | `/api/long-running/{board_id}/tick` | one manual tick (debug/testing) | | socket | `codx-junior-long-running` | step events: `tick`, `task_started`, `task_done`, `finished`, `budget_exhausted` | ### 3.6 Tool surface One new unified tool `long_running` (same pattern as `project_manager`), registered in `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` with `settings` + `session` injection: - `start` — a normal chat can turn an objective into a run ("Create a website with a and b…"). - `status` — progress/budget for the managing profile. - `finish` — **only** the run's own profile on the run's own control chat may declare completion (validated server‑side). - `add_task` — kept as a thin alias over `project_manager(action='create_task')` so the supervisor has one obvious verb. The supervisor's system prompt (new `codx/junior/profiles/long_running.profile`) states: objective, budget remaining, task table, and the rules — *split only what is needed now*, *always leave a verifiable next step*, *always end with a "how to test" task*, *call `finish` only when the objective is demonstrably achieved*. ### 3.7 Alternatives considered and rejected | Alternative | Why not | |---|---| | Keep the whole loop in memory / in the request | 30s middleware timeout; dies on restart | | Encode the run only in `kanban.json` | UI read‑modify‑write race; runtime fields are noise for the board editor | | New `LongRun` entity in `db.py` (TinyDB) | Chats already carry cost/status/board; a second entity duplicates persistence and breaks `/api/planning` | | Re‑introduce AI sub‑task generation (`generate_tasks`) | Explicitly removed by design (tasks are created with all their information) | | Drive from `Chat.mode="agent"` recursion (`AGENT_DONE_WORD`) | Single chat, no board budget, no new tasks, not resumable per task | | Celery/APScheduler worker | New infra and deployment; existing daemon‑thread pattern is enough for v1 | ### 3.8 Risks / edge cases - **Self‑expansion** → `max_tasks`, `max_iterations`, stagnation detection, budget floor. - **Board renamed by user** → state keyed by `board_id`, folder moves only through the catalogue (a rename mid‑run must pause the run). - **Two `kanban.json` writers** → only the config key is written on start/stop, and always through `ChatManager.save_kanban` with a lock/short retry. - **Money accounting drift** → always recompute `spent` from chats; the checkpoint is informational only. - **`estimation_cost` shrink** → set once per turn from `remaining` (never above it), so a resumed task cannot exceed the board budget. - **Background process disabled** (`CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND` unset) → runs sit in `running` until a worker exists: the status endpoint must surface "waiting for worker". --- ## 4. Changes Summary **New files** | File | Contents | |---|---| | `codx/junior/long_running/__init__.py` | public exports (`LongRunningService`, `LongRunningRunner`, models) | | `codx/junior/long_running/models.py` | `LongRunStatus`, `LongRunConfig`, `LongRunState`, `LongRunProgress`, request/response models (pydantic, `ConfigDict`, docs) | | `codx/junior/long_running/store.py` | state file + lock (atomic `os.replace`, `O_CREAT\|O_EXCL`, stale takeover), board config read/write helpers over `ChatManager.load_kanban/save_kanban` | | `codx/junior/long_running/service.py` | `start / pause / resume / stop / status / list`; board + control chat creation via `project_manager_tools` helpers; config↔state↔chats aggregation (`spent`, counts, current task) | | `codx/junior/long_running/runner.py` | `tick()`: recovery, task selection, `estimation_cost` push‑down, `session.chat_with_project`, supervisor turn, stop conditions, events | | `codx/junior/api/long_running.py` | the router (auto‑discovered by `discover_routers`) | | `codx/junior/tools/long_running_tools.py` | `long_running` tool (`start/status/finish/add_task`) + `LONG_RUNNING_TOOL_JSON` | | `codx/junior/profiles/long_running.profile` | supervisor instructions (objective → tasks → verify → finish) | **Modified files** | File | Change | |---|---| | `codx/junior/background.py` | add `check_long_running_runs()` + `run_long_running_tick()` and start the thread in `start_background_services` (guarded by the same flag/stop event) | | `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` | register `long_running` in `TOOLS` (`async: True`, `project_settings: True`, `session: True`) | **No changes** to `db.py`, `chat_manager.py`, `smol_agent.py`, `planning_manager.py`: `Chat.cost`/`estimation_cost`/`status_history`/`tags` (`long_run:`) already carry everything. **Out of scope (separate fix, still flagged):** the broken `codx/junior/kanban/__init__.py` import, and the duplicated/legacy handlers in `app.py` and `api/chat.py`. --- ## 5. The Changes Not written yet, deliberately: four decisions change the shape of `runner.py` and `service.py`, and getting them wrong would mean rewriting the loop. 1. **Budget unit** — cxjcoins via `Chat.estimation_cost`/`Chat.cost` (my recommendation), or a task counter ("N task turns")? 2. **Concurrency per run** — strictly one task turn at a time (my recommendation), or `max_parallel` from day one? 3. **Where the worker lives** — extend `background.py` (only active when `CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND` is set, i.e. the supervisor/background process), or an always‑on thread in the API process? 4. **Config location** — board entry `long_run` key in `kanban.json` + runtime state in `.codx/long_running/.json` (my recommendation), or a single separate file for everything? Confirm (or correct) these four and I will produce the initial version as complete file contents in the order `models.py` → `store.py` → `service.py` → `runner.py` → `api/long_running.py` → `tools/long_running_tools.py` → `background.py`/`tools/__init__.py` patches.

This module is responsible for chat persistence and management.

Besides the classic full-chat ``save_chat``, this module now exposes granular,
merge-safe message operations (``add_message``, ``update_message``,

It also provides full-text search capabilities via the ``search_chats`` method,

matching, and pagination.

Merge strategy (per message, keyed by ``doc_id``):

    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
        A[Incoming chat messages] --> C{doc_id exists in stored chat?}
        B[Stored chat messages] --> C
        C -->|No| D[Keep message]
        C -->|Yes| E{parse incoming.updated_at >= parse stored.updated_at?}
        E -->|Yes| F[Keep incoming]
        E -->|No| G[Keep stored]
        D --> H[Merged message list]
        F --> H
        G --> H
    ```

CHANGED — timestamp normalisation:
    ``updated_at`` values historically exist in TWO formats:
    ``str(datetime.now())`` (space separator, Message default) and
    ``datetime.isoformat()`` (T separator, stamped by add/update_message).
    Comparing them as raw strings is WRONG ("...T..." always beats "... ..."
    lexicographically for the same day). :func:`_parse_timestamp` parses both

1. **Request:** add long‑running tasks — a complex objective is split into sub‑tasks on a dedicated kanban board with a budget and a managing profile, processed until all done / budget exhausted / user stops, and resumable after any restart.
2. **API review:** tasks are chats (`Chat` with `board`/`column`/`status`/`cost`/`estimation_cost`), the board catalogue is `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` (`ChatManager.load_kanban/save_kanban`), budget is already enforced per chat in `smol_agent.py`, cancellation via `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY` + `POST /api/chat/cancel`, and background work runs in daemon threads from `background.py` (not in the 30s‑limited request path).
3. **Proposed design:** a run = board config (`long_run` key) + runtime state in `.codx/long_running/<board_id>.json` with a file lock; a `tick()` runner picks one actionable task at a time, pushes the remaining budget down as `estimation_cost`, and hands control to the supervisor profile when no task is actionable, which alone may call `finish`.
4. **Deliverables:** new `codx/junior/long_running/` (models, store, service, runner), `api/long_running.py` (start/pause/resume/stop/status/tick), `tools/long_running_tools.py`, a supervisor profile, plus patches to `background.py` and `tools/__init__.py`; no changes to `db.py`, `chat_manager.py`, `smol_agent.py` or `planning_manager.py`.
5. **Open before implementation:** budget unit (cxjcoins vs task count), one task at a time vs `max_parallel`, worker inside `background.py` vs an always‑on API thread, and config split across `kanban.json` + state file vs a single file — plus two pre‑existing defects to fix separately (broken `codx/junior/kanban/__init__.py` import, duplicated/legacy handlers in `app.py` and `api/chat.py`).
